_comment: The backup series (lore/drift_wood/_BACKUPS.md): one entry per series, keyed by the exact `series` string the bk_ strips carry. title/subtitle are what the title page letters; masthead says how the title is drawn on the title page; running_head is the small series mark on every later page; tagline goes under the title on the title page; credit is the printed credit line (empty for found or unsigned series). page_count is checked against the strips on disk by the validator. Read by comic_tool.py; the prompt letters the masthead on the title page and the running head elsewhere.

THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE.title: THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE
THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE.subtitle: The Timberline · an issue that never went to the copier · 1998
THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE.tagline: The cafeteria at night. The tray line moving with no one at it.
THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE.masthead: the title cut from black construction paper in tall dripping capitals and pasted across the top of the page, the school paper's name beneath it in the xeroxed masthead type, a bat-shaped cut-out where the paper's logo would be
THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE.running_head: a small black rectangle at the top corner with the word HALLOWEEN reversed out white, the page number beside it

THE FRONTIER WEEK.title: THE FRONTIER WEEK
THE FRONTIER WEEK.subtitle: Small Wood, 1871 · a western week the editor cut
THE FRONTIER WEEK.tagline: Every strip he'll be asked his name. Every strip he'll say the town's.
THE FRONTIER WEEK.masthead: the title in fat wood-type circus capitals on a weathered plank sign with two nail holes, a curl of rope around one end, the subtitle in small slab capitals on a second smaller plank hung crooked beneath it
THE FRONTIER WEEK.running_head: a tiny plank with the word FRONTIER burned into it in the top corner, the strip's weekday beside it

SLASH.title: SLASH
SLASH.subtitle: a crime story of the Oregon coast · Box 4B · sixty pages, never lettered
SLASH.masthead: the title as one wet brush stroke, the five letters made by a single diagonal slash of white through a field of black vertical rain hatching, the subtitle in small neat pen capitals in the bottom margin
SLASH.running_head: the word SLASH very small in the top-left corner in brush, one short diagonal stroke through it, the page number in the top-right

NOIR WEEK II · THE DOG DETECTIVE.title: NOIR WEEK II
NOIR WEEK II · THE DOG DETECTIVE.subtitle: THE DOG DETECTIVE · the second week, unrun
NOIR WEEK II · THE DOG DETECTIVE.tagline: It was raining. It's always raining. That's the coast.
NOIR WEEK II · THE DOG DETECTIVE.masthead: the title in heavy pulp-paperback capitals with a hard drop shadow, a fedora's silhouette resting on the last letter, THE DOG DETECTIVE beneath in a narrow condensed face, and a caption box at the page's foot with the tagline
NOIR WEEK II · THE DOG DETECTIVE.running_head: a tiny fedora in the top corner with the words NOIR WEEK II in condensed capitals beside it

THE SINKHOLE.title: THE SINKHOLE
THE SINKHOLE.subtitle: a Sunday page from a paper he never drew for · found in Box 5
THE SINKHOLE.masthead: a newspaper Sunday-section masthead in a line almost his and not his: the title in a florid serif with a section number, a dateline drawn as blocks, a small circular section logo of a street opening into a hole, and the newsprint's fold crease running straight through the title
THE SINKHOLE.running_head: the title small in the same florid serif at the top of the page with a section page number, the fold crease beneath it

RUST_CODE.BBS.title: RUST_CODE.BBS
RUST_CODE.BBS.subtitle: drawn during Message Boards · never posted
RUST_CODE.BBS.masthead: the title as a banner of phosphor-green block capitals across a gray monitor's screen, drawn in a monospaced hand with a blinking cursor after the last letter, the subtitle in green beneath it and the tagline on the line below that
RUST_CODE.BBS.running_head: a small gray rectangle in the top corner with a line of green blocks in it, the page number as two green shapes

THE RENDER WEEK.title: THE RENDER WEEK
THE RENDER WEEK.subtitle: a science-fiction week the papers declined · posted once, taken down
THE RENDER WEEK.masthead: the title in phosphor-green wireframe capitals, the first two words shaded solid and the third still an outline, a progress bar under the whole title three-quarters full, the subtitle in small type below the bar
THE RENDER WEEK.running_head: the word RENDER in tiny wireframe capitals at the top corner with a short progress bar beside it

THE LONG WAY BACK.title: THE LONG WAY BACK
THE LONG WAY BACK.subtitle: twenty-two stops on 101 · the sabbatical, 2010
THE LONG WAY BACK.tagline: He doesn't recognize himself. The reader does.
THE LONG WAY BACK.masthead: the title hand-lettered along the folds of an opened highway map, the letters crossing the creases, the coast a blue line and 101 a red line with twenty-two small dots along it and eight of them ringed, the subtitle in the map's legend box
THE LONG WAY BACK.running_head: a small numeral for the stop in a ringed dot at the top corner, a short piece of red road line through it

THE CARD IN THE DRAWER.title: THE CARD IN THE DRAWER
THE CARD IN THE DRAWER.subtitle: room twelve · a card each month from a guest never seen
THE CARD IN THE DRAWER.tagline: No numeral, no title. The card's name is the thing.
THE CARD IN THE DRAWER.masthead: the title lettered in brush capitals directly on the front of a motel nightstand drawer, the drawer's brass pull sitting in place of the letter O in DRAWER, the drawer open an inch on darkness, the subtitle in small pen capitals on the nightstand's top edge
THE CARD IN THE DRAWER.running_head: a tiny drawn drawer-front at the top corner with the card's month lettered on it

THE POMEGRANATE HOUR, 3 AM.title: THE POMEGRANATE HOUR
THE POMEGRANATE HOUR, 3 AM.subtitle: 3 AM · the lobby TV · recaps never run
THE POMEGRANATE HOUR, 3 AM.tagline: A channel the motel doesn't get.
THE POMEGRANATE HOUR, 3 AM.masthead: a television title card: the title in elegant late-night-show script across a rounded-rectangle screen, a pomegranate cut open in place of the O in HOUR with its seeds in the screen's blue spot tone, 3 AM in a clock's digits beneath, the subtitle in small capitals under the screen's bracket
THE POMEGRANATE HOUR, 3 AM.running_head: a tiny rounded screen at the top corner with 3 AM in it

CEDAR.title: CEDAR
CEDAR.subtitle: a novel of the timber country · the corner box promised it in 2017
CEDAR.tagline: Nobody in the house finds it strange.
CEDAR.masthead: the title carved into the end grain of a cedar round that fills the page, the five letters cut through the rings, one ring notched, the subtitle lettered along the bark's edge in small brush capitals, wet-on-wet cedar red and moss
CEDAR.running_head: a tiny cedar round at the top corner with the page's ring notched, the word CEDAR beside it in brush

POSTCARDS FROM THE OTHER TOWN.title: POSTCARDS FROM THE OTHER TOWN
POSTCARDS FROM THE OTHER TOWN.subtitle: a romance in eight cards · never ran
POSTCARDS FROM THE OTHER TOWN.masthead: the title lettered in a postcard's souvenir script across a card's blank front, each word in a different pastel, the subtitle on the card's divided back as the only legible line among strokes, a stamp with no numeral crooked in the corner
POSTCARDS FROM THE OTHER TOWN.running_head: a tiny stamp at the top corner with the card's numeral, the word POSTCARDS in souvenir script beside it

THE BACKWARD DIGEST.title: THE BACKWARD DIGEST
THE BACKWARD DIGEST.subtitle: after the print tech's misfold of September 30, 1999
THE BACKWARD DIGEST.tagline: The reader who reads it the usual way arrives home first.
THE BACKWARD DIGEST.masthead: the title lettered mirror-reversed in the xerox capitals of the 1997 masthead so it reads correctly only in a mirror, printed on a quarter-letter digest folded the wrong way with its staple showing, the subtitle beneath in the private washes reading the right way round
THE BACKWARD DIGEST.running_head: the word BACKWARD very small and mirror-reversed at the top corner on the wrong side of the page

THE FREQUENCY BENEATH.title: THE FREQUENCY BENEATH
THE FREQUENCY BENEATH.subtitle: after a paperback found in the library's return cart
THE FREQUENCY BENEATH.masthead: the title formed by a single oscilloscope trace on graph paper, one unbroken warm line rising and falling into each letter and then running flat off the right edge of the page, the subtitle in small ruled capitals in the graph's margin, the tagline as two shapes not a numeral
THE FREQUENCY BENEATH.running_head: a short flat trace at the top of the page with one small blip in it, no words

THE SCUMM STICK.title: THE SCUMM STICK
THE SCUMM STICK.subtitle: an adventure that doesn't exist · after the machine in the pizza window
THE SCUMM STICK.tagline: LOOK AT · PICK UP · TALK TO · USE · OPEN · GIVE · WALK TO
THE SCUMM STICK.masthead: a game's title screen in a 4:3 frame: the title in chunky sixteen-color pixel capitals over the garage doorway's silhouette, the verb bar beneath with no verb marked, the inventory strip empty, and the sentence line reading NEW GAME
THE SCUMM STICK.running_head: the title in tiny pixel capitals at the top of the 4:3 frame, the room number beside it
